item.description:
### Added - The Advanced Folder Pattern add-on learns a series that starts again each year from a complete year: where it ends, a list of numbers it skips, and how wide they are written, as `{seq:24:1}` or `{seq:5,10,15,20}`. In a folder per year it can read the names in the same folder a year before, as `Administration/2025/Tax` beside `Administration/2026/Tax`, so a new year's folder gets last year's pattern at once. Settings > Add-ons has Also read names in the same folder a year before, on by default; only names are read. - Halves after an H, as `H1` and `H2`, continue as a series of two.
### Changed - Settings > Add-ons shows each add-on as a card with its licence as a coloured badge and a switch. Selecting a card opens it and folds the others; the list fills the tab and scrolls to the card selected. What an add-on recognizes shows with an example of each field, as `{seq:4}` 1–4, coloured by kind. - Advanced Folder Pattern learns a list from one complete year whose numbers step evenly, as 2, 4, 6, 8, and such a list comes before the months. - The sidebar can be made wider, up to 400 points, and starts at 260. Each window keeps its sidebar's width, also after a restart, and a new window starts at the width last chosen. When the window is made narrower, the sidebar gives way first. The sidebar's button stands at the right over the sidebar, away from the window's buttons.
### Fixed - The Settings window is titled by the tab chosen, instead of Untitled.

### Added - The Advanced Folder Pattern add-on comes with Treewise. It recognizes more in a folder's names than the free add-on: years, quarters after a Q and months after a year that continue a series, and names that follow one of several patterns. Try it for 14 days with Try for 14 Days in Settings > Add-ons or in the overview of proposed names; after that it works with a licence key, entered with Enter Licence Key…. It is not for sale yet. - A licence key can have an end date; Settings then says until when it counts, and how many days are left in its last week. - Settings > Add-ons says what each add-on does and what it recognizes in a folder's names. - `{seq}` takes a range, a list or an open end: `{seq:2-4}`, `{seq:2,4,6,8}`, `{seq:5-}`, and its width by leading zeros or a second colon: `{seq:001-}`, `{seq:5-:3}`. - `{year:yy}` writes the year in two digits, `{folder:2}` is the folder above the one that holds the file, and `:lower`, `:upper` and `:title` write a field's text in small letters, capitals or with a capital at each word.
### Changed - A name fits a pattern with `{seq}` only when its number is one the series can give, so `Q5` no longer fits `Q{seq:4}`. - The overview says when a folder has too few names to recognize a pattern in: it needs at least 3.
### Fixed - The buttons at the foot of the overview of proposed names have room around them again, instead of touching the window's edge.

### Added - Extract All… unpacks zip, tar, `.tar.gz`, `.tar.bz2`, `.tar.xz`, 7z, rar, iso, cpio and xar archives to a new folder, from the command bar, the context menu and the File menu. Nothing lands in the destination unless the whole archive extracted. - Compress to ZIP puts an archive next to the selection and starts renaming it; Compress to also makes 7z and `.tar.gz` files. A zip or 7z leaves out `__MACOSX`, `._` files, `.DS_Store` and extended attributes. - Suggest Names for Whole Folder… in the context menu and the File menu, for a folder so full that a right click always lands on a file. - A double click opens an archive as a folder, and the sidebar's tree unfolds it. Inside it you can browse, sort, search, preview with Quick Look and copy or drag files out; Extract All extracts that archive. Zip, tar and 7z archives can be changed like a folder: add, replace, rename, move, copy, make folders and delete, with undo. A failed change leaves the archive as it was, and the first change puts a copy of the original in the Trash. Rar, iso, cpio and xar stay read-only. - The sidebar's tree opens down to the folder or archive a tab shows; Settings can turn this off. - A Go menu with Back, Forward and Enclosing Folder, as in Finder. - Edit > Spelling and Grammar checks the spelling of a name you are typing; checking while typing is off until you turn it on.
### Changed - Treewise's windows, menus, toolbar, Settings and everything in them are built the way Mac apps build them, which keeps a menu held open while a change ends from closing Treewise on macOS 26. - Settings are laid out as other Mac apps lay out theirs: labels on the left, checkboxes and menus on the right. - Treewise always opens again with the windows and tabs it had when it quit, whatever the system's setting for keeping windows says. - On macOS 26 the progress panel and the badge on a drag stand on Liquid Glass.
### Fixed - The first window opens on the main screen, not on the screen another display happened to give it. - Ending a drag over the sidebar no longer closes Treewise. - A change to a folder made while Treewise was reading it shows up, and an older reading no longer replaces a newer one. - Renaming no longer offers one-time codes from AutoFill, which on macOS 26 could take the keyboard away from the name, so that ⌥Esc and Escape seemed to do nothing. - A new archive, an extracted folder, a new folder and a renamed item are scrolled into view, also when sorting puts them far from where you were working.

### Added - Suggest Names… proposes names for a folder's files from a pattern that Treewise recognizes in the names already there, or that you type; you approve each name before anything is renamed. While renaming one file, ⌥Esc offers its proposals. - Patterns with dates in several forms, also with month names in English, Dutch and German, the folder's name, a running number per year, quarter or month, optional parts and choices between parts. A name that nearly fits the pattern is offered written right. Fixed text in an optional part, as `[ correction]`, goes into a proposal only when the file's name already has it. - Saved patterns in Settings > Names, to pick for a folder from the menu beside its pattern. A folder keeps the version it uses, is offered a newer one, and can update the saved pattern. - Add-ons give the values for a pattern, and run in a separate service without internet access. Settings > Add-ons turns them on or off and sets their order. The free add-on reads a file's date and its current name, and recognizes the patterns of a folder's names when most of its files fit one. - Settings > Names can clear what Treewise keeps for each folder you suggest names in. The settings of a folder not seen for 30 days on an attached disk go by themselves. - The address bar starts at your home folder or a cloud folder, shows This Mac as an icon, and puts the parts that do not fit in a menu.
### Changed - Settings has tabs: General, Names and Add-ons. - The home folder shows a blue house in the sidebar and the address bar, so it stands out from the folders around it.
### Fixed - Copying a folder, or moving it to another volume, keeps the folder's Finder tags and other extended attributes. - A file name with a dot but no extension, like `2026.04.28 Permit`, gets `copy` at its end when a name is taken.

### Added - About Treewise links to the website and to the source code, which is now open under the Mozilla Public License 2.0.
### Changed - Downloads and updates now come from the `mag243/treewise` repository.
